Make the transformation predictable.

My aim was to turn a recurring spreadsheet preparation task into a workflow with consistent inputs, visible rules and an agreed output shape. Excel and VBA handle the transformation; validation determines whether the result is ready for review.

  1. Prepare the source.Start with a defined batch and the mappings required by the import.
  2. Transform against the schema.Shape the output to a consistent 17-field contract rather than relying on ad hoc edits.
  3. Surface exceptions.Check mandatory values, mapping coverage, duplicates and reconciliation before accepting the output.
  4. Review and retain a trace.Keep exceptions and audit information visible so a reviewer can understand what needs attention.

This public description explains the workflow without exposing source records, account details, financial values or a private operational workbook.

The checks are part of the automation.

A file can have the right columns and still contain unusable data. I treat the validation path as part of the result, including the cases that need a person to resolve them.

Mandatory data
Identify required information that is missing before the batch is accepted.
Mapping
Surface values that do not have an agreed mapping instead of silently guessing a replacement.
Duplicates
Flag missing or duplicate output references and block export for review.
Reconciliation
Compare route row counts and totals, with review or approved exclusions for differences.
Review trail
Record exceptions and audit information so the reviewer can trace the outcome.

Current delivery stage

The saved v10 workflow is in controlled UAT. This page does not represent a production approval or an independently audited accuracy result.

Measure the complete task before claiming savings.

A short macro runtime would tell only part of the story. A useful comparison includes preparing the batch, processing it, reviewing exceptions and making corrections, with the same acceptance criteria for both methods.

  1. Use comparable batches with recorded row counts and similar exception patterns.
  2. Record manual preparation, processing, review and correction minutes.
  3. Record the same stages for the automated workflow, including human review.
  4. Check that both outputs meet the same reconciliation and quality criteria.
  5. Compare repeated paired runs before reporting a typical result.

Time savings: not yet established

I do not yet have verified paired manual and automated processing times for the current version. No hours-saved or percentage-improvement figure is claimed here.

Keep the figure connected to its scope.

The public verification record captures the evidence that can be shared. The 17-field count describes the output structure; it does not measure transaction volume, financial accuracy or time saved.
